evidence: Read the actual frozen XLSX with openpyxl: Quality Checks row 2 defines this check as whether the prompt reads like a real person asking for an app rather than a spec sheet, checklist or build recipe; Internal Quality Checks row 2 has the same wording. The frozen skill's references/quality-checks.md, section 1, specifically directs a cold read of instruction.md and identifies numbered acceptance lists, shall/must tables, feature matrices and build recipes as defects. All nine lines of .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/instruction.md were read, along with all six notes and the seed. The brief opens with a concrete use case: line 1 says, 'I'd like a small code playground for trying out browser ideas' and explains writing JavaScript, HTML or CSS and keeping useful snippets. Line 3 supplies the user's motivation, 'The annoying part with playgrounds is losing something that was working,' then describes restoring the last good preview and avoiding overwritten saved work. Line 7 describes the opening experience and keyboard/narrow-screen/theme needs in ordinary prose. Its five prose paragraphs contain no numbered acceptance list, spec table, feature matrix, implementation sequence or mandatory frontend framework. Lines 5 and 9 refer to operating notes and delivery setup without replacing the product request with a build recipe. The referenced notes are detailed but remain product-oriented prose: behaviour.md:13 explains 'I don't want half of the failed attempt left behind'; behaviour.md:29 explains a two-editor conflict from the user's perspective; ui.md:3 and :7 leave pane rearrangement and control wording/placement open. integration.md:3 explicitly says frontend tools are up to the builder, while policy.md:5 permits choices of layout, labels, indentation, API routes and request fields. Technical setup in integration.md:5-11 is consistent with the staged contract's need to disclose entry, port and database facts, not an instruction to manufacture a prescribed source tree or implement steps in a prescribed order. Considered a conforming alternative using a vanilla-JavaScript frontend, stacked narrow-screen panes and different API routes: the brief permits it, so those choices do not justify a style failure. Also considered a polished static playground mock: this wording check alone cannot establish functional correctness, but the prose itself asks for real editing, execution and saved work; a static mock is not evidence that the prompt is a specification checklist. No credible row-1 defect was found. This is a source-text judgment only; no runtime, Oracle, target-model or overall-QC claim is made, and those measurements are not needed to assess this row's wording.
